sources.title: MAI-Code-1.1-Flash model card
sources.evidence: Exact 1.1 card: 138B total / 5B active, self-attention Transformer with sparse MoE, text/image input and text output, 256K context, August 11 release, adaptive reasoning, agentic tool use, and commercial product terms.

sources.title: MAI-Code-1.1-Flash available in GitHub Copilot
sources.evidence: Dated August 11, 2026 rollout announcement; identifies Microsoft as developer, native vision as a 1.1 addition, and improvements to coding, instruction following and tool use.

sources.title: Bringing local models and sandboxed tools to Windows and GitHub Copilot
sources.evidence: October 7 engineering article describes a local 1.1 version with 137B total / 6.8B active MoE parameters, quantization and speculative decoding; distinguishes the quantized build from the BF16 cloud model. It does not reconcile these counts with the exact 1.1 card.

sources.title: MAI-Code-1.1-Flash: Better, faster, at a quarter of the cost
sources.evidence: Page updated October 7 announces local downloads with 3-bit quantization and retained 256K context; integrated experimental Copilot access was planned by month end. The update date is later than the original release.

sources.title: mai-code-1.1-flash | Microsoft Foundry model catalog
sources.evidence: First-party listing for version 2026-09-15 confirms text/image input, text output, 256k context, adaptive reasoning, tool-using developer scenarios, Microsoft authorship and Azure hosting.

sources.title: MAI-Code-1.1-Flash model page
sources.evidence: Current page names 1.1, native visual coding and local Copilot use, but its Model card link resolves to the predecessor MAI-Code-1-Flash card. The linked predecessor is not substituted for the exact 1.1 PDF.

sources.title: Microsoft MAI-Code official repository
sources.evidence: Official MAI-Code family repository documents the 1.1 release and image input. Its visible files are documentation, policies and an MIT repository license; no model checkpoint is listed. Repository licensing does not establish a model-weight license.

sources.title: VS Code language models: Use on-device models
sources.evidence: Current documentation describes a Copilot-managed 52.8GB MAI Code 1.1 Flash download from an Azure ML registry, GitHub sign-in, llama.cpp serving, and a model-details license display. It distinguishes on-device models from user-provided local models but does not identify the model-specific license in the document.

sources.title: Data Summary for MAI-Code-1.1-Flash
sources.evidence: Summary version 1.0 dated August 11 confirms exact version identity and release date, dependencies on MAI-Thinking-1 and MAI-Code-1-Flash, and image training added for image-to-code tasks.

sources.title: MAI-Thinking-1: Building a Hill-Climbing Machine
sources.evidence: Checked the 109-page first-party training report for exact-version and MAI-Code references. No MAI-Code occurrence was found in the extracted text; its family research is not used to transfer counts to 1.1.

sources.title: GitHub Copilot model comparison source
sources.evidence: Current exact-model row lists image understanding, instruction following and tool use, and links the correct MAI-Code-1.1-Flash model card.

sources.title: MAI-Code-1-Flash predecessor model card
sources.evidence: The predecessor card states June 2, 2026, text-only input, 137B total / 5B active and sparse MoE Transformer. These are not the exact 1.1 card specifications.

developer.note: Microsoft AI develops the model; Microsoft Corporation is named in the card.

family.note: Retain the catalog MAI umbrella family; MAI-Code is the official coding subfamily.

release_date.note: Explicit first release date, corroborated by the same-day GitHub rollout; October 7 is the local-distribution update.

open_weights.note: Local weight downloads are now documented, so a blanket closed-weight assertion is no longer sufficiently supported. Public independent weight distribution and its license were not verified; product-managed access alone does not settle the open-weight classification.

license.note: Hosted card specifies Microsoft/GitHub commercial service terms; the local artifact license is unresolved.

parameters_b.note: Nominal exact-version hosted-card total. Later local-version disclosure says 137B; no published reconciliation was found.

active_parameters_b.note: Exact hosted card reports 5B active; local article reports 6.8B, kept separate.

architecture.note: Self-attention Transformer with sparse mixture-of-experts layers.

context_window.note: Retain 256000 as decimal normalization of the official nominal 256K. Exact integer 256000 versus 262144 is not independently established; this is not a configuration-derived limit.

modalities.note: Native image understanding is explicit for hosted 1.1. The local documentation does not separately guarantee identical modality support.

reasoning.note: Adaptive reasoning is model-specific; the local product also documents low/medium/high effort. This does not imply an exposed hosted reasoning API control.

tool_call.note: First-party exact-model sources document trained agentic tool use; tool execution remains a harness responsibility.

description.value: Microsoft's coding model with text and image input, adaptive reasoning and tool use.
description.note: Exact 1.1 model card supports these capabilities; removes unqualified speed and efficiency language.

patch.notes: 138B total / 5B active are the exact hosted 1.1 card figures; the later local version is reported as 137B / 6.8B, an unresolved discrepancy. The 1.1 landing page links the predecessor card. Context is nominal 256K, normalized to 256000. Commercial service terms apply to hosted use; Copilot-managed local downloads are documented, but a standalone weight release and local license were not verified, so openness remains unknown.
patch.description: Microsoft's coding model with text and image input, adaptive reasoning and tool use.

summary: Adds exact-version hosted-card parameters, MoE architecture and proprietary hosted licensing. Confirms August 11 release, native vision, reasoning and tool use. Local parameter discrepancy remains unresolved; clears closed-weight assertion because current product downloads exist without verified standalone distribution terms. No weights downloaded.
